Reports indicate that Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, suggesting that this cooling technology may play a more important role in its future hardware product lineup. Here are the details.

Apple Doubles Down on Vapor Chamber Cooling Technology

Tipster Fixed Focus Digital posted on Weibo, claiming that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber order volume," and added that this move "may be in preparation for enhanced cooling for its first foldable iPhone, as well as the next-generation 20th anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling on the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address cooling issues found in previous models.

The vapor chamber works by evaporating a small amount of liquid near the heat source, then condensing it at a cooler location to spread the heat over a larger surface area, before returning the liquid to repeat the cycle.

You can see how it actually works in this great video from Know Art below:

Although the Weibo post speculated that Apple's increased orders are aimed at the iPhone Ultra and the 20th anniversary iPhone expected in 2027, looking at the timeline, it seems more reasonable for this year's product lineup to adopt the technology.

Reports indicate that Apple has asked suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, an increase from the previous target of 7 to 8 million, alongside orders for approximately 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling.

The increase in orders comes amid reports that Apple has resolved previous issues with hinges and production yield rates, clearing the way for higher production targets ahead of its September launch.
